plan.search_reasoning: The upstream plan contains 10 queries across 5 source-type channels but uses overly rigid quoted phrase constructions (e.g., "Mpox DRC 2024" as a literal phrase) that are unlikely to match real document text, and the date-range string "2024-08-01-2024-08-31" embedded in query text will not improve recall. The bounds allow only 4 queries in this iteration and 10 total across 2 iterations, so queries must be high-yield and cover the most authoritative source types first. Priority order: (1) WHO situation reports / AFRO regional office — the primary international authoritative source for DRC Mpox weekly/monthly data; (2) DRC Ministry of Health / INRB (Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale) — the national authority, which publishes in French; (3) WHO Disease Outbreak News and PAHO/AFRO dashboards — structured international reporting; (4) News/media aggregation for subnational granularity and corroboration. French-language queries are essential because DRC's national health communications are primarily in French ("variole du singe" or "mpox" in French). August 2024 was a period of declared Mpox public health emergency of international concern (PHEIC), making WHO AFRO and WHO HQ situation reports especially likely to contain weekly epidemiological data with province-level breakdowns. Literal phrase quotes are relaxed to improve recall; time anchors use natural language ("August 2024") rather than hyphenated date strings.

top_result_summaries.title: Situation Report: Mpox Spreads in Africa | NETEC
top_result_summaries.snippet: + Emergency Medical Services (EMS) Featured Resources. + Consulting for Emergency Medical Services (EMS). ## Clade I Mpox Outbreak in the DRC. The outbreak has spread to neighboring countries, including the Republic of the Congo, Central African Republic, Burundi, Rwanda, and Uganda, with confirmed or presumed cases linked to the DRC. While clade I MPXV is endemic to the DRC, the widespread transmission occurring in this outbreak and spread to neighboring countries is unusual and highlights the need for heightened surveillance and preparedness. Clade I MPXV, endemic to the DRC, is known for being more transmissible and causing more severe infections compared to clade II MPXV, which led to the global mpox outbreak in 2022. Health care providers should remain vigilant for mpox in patients with signs symptoms and symptoms consistent with mpox and recent travel history to the DRC or neighboring countries. Though no cases of clade I mpox have been reported outside central and eastern Africa, the CDC emphasizes the importance of preparedness and early detection to prevent further spread.

top_result_summaries.title: Mpox - Democratic Republic of the Congo
top_result_summaries.snippet: # Mpox - Democratic Republic of the Congo. In December 2022, the Democratic Republic of the Congo declared a national outbreak of mpox and an incident management system has been in place since February 2023, based on the increasing number of reported cases. The continuing development of the mpox outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains concerning due to the continuing high incidence of mpox reported in endemic areas of the country in recent years with high case fatality, the geographic expansion to previously unaffected areas, the appearance of a novel strain of clade I MPXV, the observed sustained community transmission driven by sexual transmission and other forms of close physical contact in the eastern part of the country, resource constraints to respond over such a wide geographic area, limited public awareness of mpox, the insufficient availability of treatment kits and lack of vaccines to date, multiple competing public health priorities, and insecurity.

top_result_summaries.title: Health Alert Network (HAN) - 00513 | Mpox Caused by Human-to-Human Transmission of Monkeypox Virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with Spread to Neighboring Countries
top_result_summaries.snippet: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is issuing this Health Alert Network (HAN) Health Update to provide additional information about the outbreak of monkeypox virus (MPXV) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC); the first Health Advisory about this outbreak was released in December 2023. While clade I MPXV is endemic, or naturally occurring, in DRC, the current outbreak is more widespread than any previous DRC outbreak and has resulted in clade I monkeypox transmission to some neighboring countries. The Republic of the Congo (ROC), which borders DRC to the west, declared a clade I monkeypox outbreak in April 2024, and there have been confirmed cases in the Central African Republic (CAR). In late July 2024, Burundi, Rwanda, and Uganda, which sit on the eastern border of DRC, reported confirmed cases of monkeypox, with some cases having linkages to DRC. Rwanda and Uganda have confirmed these cases are due to clade I MPXV; in Burundi, clade-specific testing is underway, but cases are presumed to be clade I due to DRC’s proximity.

top_result_summaries.title: Mpox outbreak in DR Congo: What to know | Doctors Without Borders - USA
top_result_summaries.snippet: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo. # Mpox outbreak in DR Congo: What to know. A recent surge of mpox (formerly known as monkeypox) infections in DR Congo is cause for alarm. Here’s what to know and why we need a comprehensive response. While epidemic outbreaks are generally concentrated in the center and northwest of the country, confirmed cases of mpox have now been reported in the eastern provinces of South and North Kivu, where almost a million displaced people are living in overcrowded conditions. The epidemic now affects all provinces in the country and, following a genetic mutation in South Kivu, has been causing uninterrupted human-to-human transmission of the virus for months. Our teams are on the ground in South Kivu, North Kivu, Equateur, and South Ubangi provinces to support the local health authorities. On August 14, the World Health Organization (WHO) director-general declared that the surge of mpox cases in DRC and a growing number of countries in Africa constitutes a public health emergency of international concern.
